dsl_functions.label: Average (AVG) function
dsl_functions.description: Calculates the average (mean) value of a numeric variable. Typical natural language questions: 'average age of users', 'average price of products', 'mean salary of employees'.

dsl_functions.label: Sum (SUM) function
dsl_functions.description: Sums the numeric values of a variable across all matching rows. Typical questions: 'total sales', 'sum of quantities', 'total revenue'.

dsl_functions.label: Count (COUNT) function
dsl_functions.description: Counts the number of values or rows. Typical questions: 'how many orders', 'number of users in each city', 'count of products in a category'.

dsl_functions.label: Minimum (MIN) function
dsl_functions.description: Returns the smallest numeric value of a variable. Typical questions: 'minimum price of products', 'youngest user age'.

dsl_functions.label: Maximum (MAX) function
dsl_functions.description: Returns the largest numeric value of a variable. Typical questions: 'maximum order total', 'oldest user age'.

dsl_functions.label: Absolute value function
dsl_functions.description: Returns the absolute value of a numeric expression. Typical questions: 'absolute difference between planned and actual quantity'.

dsl_functions.label: Round function
dsl_functions.description: Rounds a numeric value to the nearest integer or to a given number of decimals.

dsl_functions.label: String length function
dsl_functions.description: Returns the length of a string in characters. Typical questions: 'names longer than 20 characters'.

dsl_functions.label: Substring check function
dsl_functions.description: Checks whether a string contains a given substring. Typical questions: 'products whose name contains "phone"'.

dsl_clauses.label: Filter clause (WHERE condition)
dsl_clauses.description: Filters results using a boolean condition such as 'age > 18', 'price < 100', or 'city = "London"'. In natural language this corresponds to phrases like 'where', 'only users older than 18', 'products whose price is greater than 100', 'customers living in London'.

dsl_clauses.label: Optional pattern clause
dsl_clauses.description: Marks a part of the pattern as optional. Equivalent to SPARQL OPTIONAL. Used for questions like 'list all users and optionally their email if available'.

dsl_clauses.label: GROUP BY clause
dsl_clauses.description: Groups results by one or more variables so that aggregate functions like SUM, COUNT, or AVG can be applied per group. Typical questions: 'number of users in each city', 'total sales per customer'.

dsl_clauses.label: HAVING-like group filter clause
dsl_clauses.description: Applies a filter condition on grouped results, similar to SQL HAVING. Example questions: 'customers with more than 5 orders', 'cities with at least 100 users'.

dsl_modifiers.label: ORDER BY modifier
dsl_modifiers.description: Orders the result set by one or more expressions. Typical questions: 'top 10 most expensive products', 'list users sorted by age'.

dsl_modifiers.label: LIMIT modifier
dsl_modifiers.description: Limits the number of rows returned. Typical questions: 'top 10', 'first 5 results'.

dsl_modifiers.label: OFFSET modifier
dsl_modifiers.description: Skips the first n results. Used for pagination, for example 'skip the first 10 results and then return the next 10'.

dsl_modifiers.label: DISTINCT modifier
dsl_modifiers.description: Eliminates duplicate result rows. Typical questions: 'distinct cities of users', 'unique product categories'.

TruyVanCHONJ_KW.label: SELECT query
TruyVanCHONJ_KW.description: Returns variable bindings based on a WHERE pattern. Equivalent to SPARQL SELECT.

ProjectionList.description: List of variables or expressions (including aggregates) to return.

WhereClause.description: Main WHERE block containing triple patterns and filter/optional clauses.

GroupByClause?.description: Optional GROUP BY clause when using aggregates on groups.

HavingClause?.description: Optional HAVING-like clause to filter grouped results.

Modifiers?.description: Optional DISTINCT / ORDER BY / LIMIT / OFFSET modifiers applied after WHERE/GROUP BY.

TruyVanCHONJ_KW.example_dsl: CHONJ_KW ?city (DEMM_JJ(?person) AS ?userCount) NOII_MA_KK { ?person :livesIn ?city } NHOMM_THEO_YY ?city DIEU_KIEN_NHOMM_PP(DEMM_JJ(?person) > 100) SAP_XXEP_THEO_KK ?userCount GIOI_HHAN_RR 10

TruyVanXAY_DUNGWJ.label: CONSTRUCT query
TruyVanXAY_DUNGWJ.description: Builds new RDF triples from existing data patterns. Equivalent to SPARQL CONSTRUCT.

ConstructTemplate.description: Template of triples to construct from the matched WHERE patterns.

WhereClause.description: WHERE patterns that select existing data to build new triples from.

TruyVanHOIQQ_YZ.label: ASK query
TruyVanHOIQQ_YZ.description: Checks if a pattern has at least one match. Returns a boolean result. Equivalent to SPARQL ASK.

triple_pattern_spec.description: Basic triple pattern. The predicate (:property) must be one of the properties defined in the domain ontology. The subject and object should be variables or resources compatible with the property's domain and range.
